key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio strongly improves Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings by reducing porosity and roughness while boosting adhesion.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical process-control lever for producing denser, better-adhering corrosion-resistant coatings on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coating onto AISI 321 austenitic stainless steel.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Monitored spraying with Accuraspray 4.0 and measured porosity, roughness, microhardness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: At O2/C2H2 = 1.2, porosity fell from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and adhesion rose from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa; peak microhardness was 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The optimal setting may depend on substrate, spray distance, and diagnostic calibration, so these results should be validated for other geometries and service conditions.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
